corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Folley differentiates unrestricted possible-world counterfactuality from the consequence argument’s fixed-history-and-laws accessibility relation, exposing why Hawkins’s sourcehood defense changes modal domains instead of answering the narrower alternatives challenge. Principal limitation: Although exceptionally explicit and charitable, the reply underdevelops the inference from fixed history and laws to inaccessible alternatives, leaving the consequence argument’s transfer principles undefended. Live burden: Hawkins must demonstrate that agential sourcehood supplies responsibility-relevant possibility while antecedent history and natural laws remain fixed, or explain why broader cross-world variation answers that constrained question. Locked score: This decisive, disciplined diagnostic reply merits the very strong 85–94 band because exceptional coherence, responsiveness, precision, and representational charity substantially outweigh its localized omission of a deeper consequence-argument defense.
